items.title: LATEST: With 51.8% of votes counted in Israel's election, neither bloc has a majority.  Netanyahu's bloc has 55 seats, the opposition 49 and the Arab-led parties 16, against the 61…
items.summary_raw: LATEST: With 51.8% of votes counted in Israel's election, neither bloc has a majority.  Netanyahu's bloc has 55 seats, the opposition 49 and the Arab-led parties 16, against the 61 needed to govern.  Likud leads the partial count with 27 seats, ahead of Eisenkot's Yashar (21), the Joint List (12), Bennett's Together (11), and The Democrats and United Torah Judaism (9 each).  The overnight exit-poll updates also moved toward Netanyahu.  Kan 11 now gives his bloc 51 seats, Channel 12 gives it 52 and Channel 13 gives it 51, all up from 50, while the opposition dropped to 49–51.  Channel 14, which is close to Netanyahu, is the only one that now projects him a majority, with 62 seats.  The opposition and both Arab parties together would reach 65.  However, the Joint List has offered only outside support, so any anti-Netanyahu government would have to be a minority government or depend on parties from the other bloc.  Netanyahu, for his part, is 6 seats short in the current count, so the remaining 48% of votes and which small parties clear the 3.25% threshold could decide the outcome.

items.title: Trump says government to ‘terminate’ Biden-era methane emissions rules
items.summary_raw:
Critics warn of climate danger as president in Texas claims change will save companies and consumers billions

Donald Trump announced his administration is “terminating” Biden-era regulations holding oil and gas companies accountable for large leaks of planet-warming methane during a rally in Lubbock, Texas, on Tuesday evening.

Trump said during a campaign rally in Texas that the change would save consumers and energy producers $45bn and unlock 210 million barrels of oil – equivalent to about 10 days of US petroleum consumption. “Tonight, I’m officially terminating Biden’s expensive and unnecessary methane regulations to save consumers and energy producers,” Trump said, lifting what he called “crippling regulations on methane that caused prices to skyrocket” for small oil and gas operators.

items.title: Greece, Egypt, Cyprus, Bahrain, UAE and EU Issue Joint Statement at UN, Call Turkey-Libya Maritime Deal “Null and Void” (Video)
items.summary_raw:
NEW YORK – “The memorandum remains null and void, is contrary to international law, and cannot serve as a lawful basis for the delimitation of maritime zones or produce legal effects for third States,” Foreign Minister George Gerapetritis stressed as he delivered a joint statement on behalf of Greece, Egypt, Cyprus, Bahrain, the United Arab Emirates and the European Union. The statement concerns the recent decision by Libya’s House of Representatives to ratify the 2019 Turkey-Libya memorandum on the delimitation of maritime areas of jurisdiction in the Mediterranean, which, it notes, “raises serious concerns for regional security and stability.” According to the joint statement, the decision also highlights a broader challenge to the international legal order: “the need to ensure that arbitrary bilateral agreements do not undermine established rules of international law or prejudice the rights of third States.”

They impacted the eastern suburbs of Kyiv, striking currently unknown targets. Some of the missiles missed their targets and fell in open areas, due to the low accuracy of modified S-400s.  Ukraine launched two interceptor missiles of an unknown type (not Patriot), but was unable to shoot down any of the 8 ballistic missiles used.

items.summary_raw: Nuno Felix RT @BrunoTertrais: Am not sure it's that simple. A NATO operation based on (but not limited to) F35A-B61Mod12 would probably have a high probability to reach targets in Russia. And US vs. Fr mission profiles are different.  NATO’s U.S.-led nuclear sharing relies on B-61 gravity nuclear bombs, designed in the 1960s to stop Soviet tank divisions sprinting from East Germany. They have become increasingly obsolete in a modern war—and pose a limited threat to the Russian homeland given advances in Russian air defenses. France’s ASMP-A nuclear-tipped cruise missiles on Rafales, by contrast, are designed to strike Russia’s main cities and have a high chance of reaching their targets, creating an entirely different level of deterrence. The very nature of French nuclear doctrine and its nuclear arsenal makes it in some ways more threatening to Russia, said Nicole Grajewski, an expert on Russia and nuclear affairs at Sciences Po university in Paris. “The B-61 bombs are not instruments for war fighting, they’re pretty much instruments of political assurance,” she said. “The French nuclear arsenal, by contrast, can reach Russia.” @NicoleGrajewski   https://www.wsj.com/world/europe/f

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian has called on Muslim countries to strengthen regional cooperation against what he described as “Israeli aggression” and US-backed efforts to divide the Middle East, as senior Saudi, Pakistani and Turkish officials met with him in Tehran.

During the meeting with Saudi Defence Minister Khalid bin Salman, Pakistan’s army chief Asim Munir and Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin, Pezeshkian condemned Israeli attacks on Gaza, Lebanon, Iran and other parts of the region.

He said Iran was not seeking nuclear weapons but insisted on its right to pursue peaceful nuclear activities under the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty.

He also criticised what he called “contradictory US policies”

items.title: Typhoon Champi declared strongest storm of year so far
items.summary_raw:
One dead and 527 injured as winds of up to 185mph hit Taiwan and southern Japan, while Greece issues flood alerts

Typhoon Champi was declared the strongest storm of the year so far after recording sustained winds of 185mph last week. From late Thursday to early Saturday, the typhoon battered Taiwan and Japan’s southern islands. Champi approached the east coast of Taiwan before the centre of the storm turned south along the Yilan County coastline, looping offshore and then tracking northwards away from the island. The storm brought gusts of up to 141mph and 48-hour rainfall totals of more than 620mm to parts of Yilan.

So far, the death toll remains at one, with 527 reported injured. There were widespread power outages, with more than 288,000 houses having no electricity at one point, although most had since been reconnected. Champi has been downgraded to a tropical storm as it rapidly weakens to the south-west of Japan’s mainland on Monday.

items.title: State Department Calls Announcement of Turkey-Libya Memorandum’s Ratification “Provocative”
items.summary_raw:
ATHENS – The U.S. State Department has described as “provocative” the announcement that the House of Representatives in eastern Libya had ratified the Turkey-Libya maritime memorandum, saying it has heightened tensions in the region and stressing that the U.S. position on the issue has not changed. The new statement, issued in response to a question from Kathimerini, follows a statement on Wednesday, October 21, in which the U.S. State Department encouraged negotiations to resolve maritime disputes, highlighting the economic benefits of a settlement. In its latest response, the department added an explicit condemnation of the announcement of the memorandum’s ratification while reiterating its call for bilateral dialogue between Greece and Turkey. Between the two statements, the Hellenic American Leadership Council (HALC), in a letter to U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio, had called on the State Department to take a clear public position against the Turkey-Libya memorandum.

Sadiq Khan has been trying to pedestrianise Oxford Street since he first became the mayor of London in 2016. On Monday, after numerous setbacks, his plan will finally come to fruition. The busiest stretch of the nation’s famous shopping street will be closed to traffic in a scheme designed to improve the area and make it more attractive to pedestrians. It should be an emblematic case study in making cities greener, less congested, more inviting places to live and visit.

items.title: Türkiye has completed the tender to reconstruct the historic Ani Bridge on its border with Armenia.  The 10th-century Silk Road bridge spans the Arpaçay River, which forms the bord…
items.summary_raw: Türkiye has completed the tender to reconstruct the historic Ani Bridge on its border with Armenia.  The 10th-century Silk Road bridge spans the Arpaçay River, which forms the border between the two countries, at the UNESCO-listed Ani archaeological site in Kars province.   Originally about 80 meters long with a single 31-meter arch, the bridge once served as a customs checkpoint, but its arch collapsed in 1807, leaving only a pier on each bank.   Türkiye and Armenia signed a protocol on the reconstruction in Yerevan in May.   The project is seen as a concrete confidence-building step in the normalization process launched in 2022, as the two countries still have no diplomatic relations and their land border has been closed since 1993.

items.title: Russia denies plans to evacuate staff working at Iran's Bushehr nuclear plant
items.summary_raw:
Russia denies plans to evacuate staff working at Iran's Bushehr nuclear plant

Russia’s embassy in Tehran has denied reports that Russian embassy staff and specialists working at the Bushehr nuclear power plant are preparing to leave Iran.

“Neither embassy staff nor Russian specialists at the Bushehr nuclear power plant have any plans to evacuate. Work continues as normal,” the embassy said in a statement, dismissing reports to the contrary as “FAKES”.

Bushehr, Iran’s only operating nuclear power plant, has come under repeated attack during the ongoing US-Israeli war on Iran. Satellite imagery released in July showed damage inside the complex.

Iran’s Foreign Ministry spokesperson, Esmaeil Baqaei, has said that France, Germany and the UK, known as the E3, and Middle Eastern foreign ministers must examine the root causes of military conflict in the region.

In Istanbul, the European foreign ministers underlined the urgent need for diplomacy concerning the US-Israel war on Iran. But Baqaei said diplomacy should not be reduced to a public relations tool and such forums must examine examine the root causes of the conflict.

He condemned the alleged double standards of the E3 regarding their inaction in the face of US and Israeli military aggression against Iran, their comprehensive support for Israel, and their destructive approaches towards Iran’s nuclear issue.

According to General Selçuk Bayraktaroğlu, Chief of the Turkish General Staff, the Turkish Armed Forces aim to produce five million one-way attack drones within the next five years, reaching a total of ten million over ten years. The ambitious plan translates into an average production rate of approximately one million drones annually, reflecting Ankara’s intention to prioritize mass production and the availability of large numbers of relatively inexpensive unmanned weapons.  The scale of Turkey’s proposed production program reflects one of the clearest lessons of the war in Ukraine. Modern warfare increasingly depends not only on sophisticated weapons but also on the ability to manufacture and replace enormous quantities of expendable drones. items.title: Turkey warns against renewed attack on Iran, says diplomacy only way
items.summary_raw:
Turkey warns against renewed attack on Iran, says diplomacy only way

Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan cautioned on Friday against any renewed attack on Iran, saying such a move would exacerbate tensions and further expand the conflict.

Diplomacy and dialogue are the only way to end the war, Fidan told the press after meeting with foreign ministers from Egypt, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Germany, France, Britain and Italy.

"A military intervention on Iran is not in any way a solution. Nobody approves this at the moment," he added.

French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot also said after Friday's meetings that renewed escalation between Iran and the United States would only have losers and raise oil prices.

items.summary_raw: Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan hosted the first joint meeting of the R4 and E3 foreign ministers in Istanbul, bringing together regional and European powers to discuss crises across the Middle East and beyond.   The R4 group of Türkiye, Egypt, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia met with the E3 of Britain, France and Germany, with Italy also joining at Ankara’s initiative.   Attendees included Germany’s Johann Wadephul, Britain’s Ed Miliband, France’s Jean-Noël Barrot, Egypt’s Badr Abdelatty, Pakistan’s Ishaq Dar, Saudi Arabia’s Faisal bin Farhan and Italy’s Antonio Tajani.   The agenda covered the Palestinian issue, including settlement expansion, settler violence and the two-state solution, as well as security in the Strait of Hormuz, Yemen, and efforts to end the Russia-Ukraine war and prevent spillover into the Black Sea.   Fidan was expected to stress “regional ownership” of security and greater international pressure on Israel.

items.title: EPA has failed to tackle cancer-linked pesticide pollution, lawsuit alleges
items.summary_raw:
Suit alleges EPA has for decades failed under the Clean Water Act to address surface-water atrazine pollution

A new lawsuit asks a federal judge to order the Trump administration to address widespread pollution from the hormone-disrupting pesticide atrazine – which has regularly been found at levels that threaten wildlife and human health.

The cancer-linked chemical is now contaminating nearly 25%, or about 860,000 miles, of all continental US rivers, according to a recent review of federal records. The waterways cover more than 20% of surface drinking water intakes across the country, and more than 675,000 private and commercial wells.

items.summary_raw:
People succumbed to heat at highest rates in Malta, Italy and Hungary, with health issues, loneliness and poverty exacerbating toll

Heat killed a record 50,000 people in European cities this summer, new research suggests, with scientists blaming climate breakdown for two in every three of the deaths.

Morgues and funeral homes filled with bodies from June to August as the heat added by planet-baking pollution cut short an extra 32,000 lives in urban areas, the researchers found. Hot days pushed vulnerable bodies into overdrive and warm nights prevented them from recovering.

items.title: Almost every shallow-water coral reef on the planet faces ecosystem collapse by 2075, UN advisors say
items.summary_raw:
Assessment finds global heating is endangering 96% of coral reefs across 80 countries – a figure scientists say should serve as a ‘wake-up call’

  • Sign up for climate and environment editor Adam Morton’s free Clear Air newsletter here

Almost every shallow-water coral reef on the planet, including Australia’s Great Barrier Reef, faces a high risk of ecosystem collapse before 2075 because of global heating, according to an assessment by United Nations nature advisers.

About 24% of the planet’s reefs across more than 80 countries are already critically endangered, the assessment said, but when the expected impacts of global heating were added this rose to 96%.

items.title: Marine life in Gulf of Mexico has still not fully recovered from 2010 BP oil spill
items.summary_raw:
New study reveals dramatic population drops in fish, cephalopods and more after the Deepwater Horizon spill

Marine life in the Gulf of Mexico plummeted by about 60% after BP’s 2010 Deepwater Horizon oil spill and has still not fully recovered, according to a new study.

The April 2010 explosion of an offshore drilling unit 50 miles off the Louisiana coast triggered the largest marine oil spill in history, releasing 134m gallons of oil into the ocean. According to the study published Monday in PNAS, the disaster – which also killed 11 people and injured 17 others – led to the “sudden, severe and persistent declines in the abundance” of marine life for more than a decade.

items.title: 'Null and void:' Egypt condemns Turkey-Libya maritime deal, reaffirms pact with Greece
items.summary_raw:
'Null and void:' Egypt condemns Turkey-Libya maritime deal, reaffirms pact with Greece

Egypt has declared a contentious maritime deal sealed by Turkey and eastern Libya as “null and void, absolutely”, reaffirming its commitment to an agreement it sealed with Greece.

Egypt’s foreign ministry on Wednesday “reiterated that the memorandum is null and void, carries no legal effect, and that its ratification by the Libyan House of Representatives entails no legal consequences whatsoever for Egypt”, according to a statement.

Egypt’s statement marks a show of support for Greece, a longtime partner in the Eastern Mediterranean, and underscores Cairo’s own reservations about the Turkish agreement, which directly contradicts one it reached with Athens.

items.title: Kaja Kallas Tells Hakan Fidan Turkish-Libyan Memorandum Violates Sovereign Rights of Third Countries
items.summary_raw:
BRUSSELS – The Libyan Parliament’s ratification of the illegal Turkish-Libyan memorandum was at the center of talks held Wednesday between EU High Representative for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy Kaja Kallas and Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan. According to Kallas’ statement, the EU’s top diplomat raised the issue with Fidan, stressing that the Turkey-Libya Memorandum of Understanding on maritime zones violates the sovereign rights of third countries. Kallas’ intervention came just hours after European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and European Council President Antonio Costa sent Ankara a strong message in support of Greece over the Turkish-Libyan memorandum ratified by the Libyan Parliament. Both leaders emphatically stressed that the memorandum is incompatible with international law and is null and void.

The post Kaja Kallas Tells Hakan Fidan Turkish-Libyan Memorandum Violates Sovereign Rights of Third Countries appeared first on The National Herald.</

items.summary_raw:
This foolish decision undermines hopes that this government will take the necessary steps the climate crisis demands

When the news broke that the UK government had approved the Jackdaw gasfield, I was at a Guardian climate event at the Royal Geographical Society. Appropriately, the theme suggested by readers was what can the public actually do in the face of what feels like paralysing climate doom?

There is so much going on that is hopeful: biodiversity tracking, river protection, rewilding. Shruti Suresh, from the independent watchdog Global Witness, told those in attendance that if they wanted to effect change, they should protest against Jackdaw and the Rosebank oilfield project. The message was so well understood that it didn’t need labouring. The mood in the room when the news came in was one of audible dismay. People had just watched the minister for climate transition declare that she could see the challenges ahead and was ready for them.
